# OSS Knowledge Base Update Proposal: `hyper` Crate

---

## Crate Overview

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| **Crate** | `hyper` |
| **Repository** | https://github.com/hyperium/hyper |
| **Total Downloads** | ~637.2M |
| **Recent Downloads** | ~131.1M |
| **Ecosystem Role** | Foundational HTTP library for Rust; underpins `reqwest`, `axum`, `warp`, `tonic`, and much of the Rust web ecosystem |

---

## Known Vulnerabilities (Proposed KB Rows)

| # | ID(s) | Summary | Severity | Affected Versions | Fixed In | Category |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **CVE-2020-35863** / GHSA-h3qr-rq2j-74w4 / RUSTSEC-2020-0008 | HTTP Request Smuggling — GET requests with bodies accepted without `Transfer-Encoding` or `Content-Length`, enabling header injection and CORS bypass | **CRITICAL** | 0.11.0 – < 0.12.34 | 0.12.34 | Request Smuggling |
| 2 | **CVE-2021-21299** / GHSA-6hfq-h8hq-87mf / RUSTSEC-2021-0020 | HTTP Request Smuggling — multiple `Transfer-Encoding` headers incorrectly accepted as chunked | **MODERATE** | 0.12.0 – < 0.12.36, 0.13.0 – < 0.13.10, 0.14.0 – < 0.14.3 | 0.12.36 / 0.13.10 / 0.14.3 | Request Smuggling |
| 3 | **CVE-2021-32714** / GHSA-5h46-h7hh-c6x9 / RUSTSEC-2021-0079 | Integer overflow in chunked Transfer-Encoding chunk-size parsing; truncation enables data loss or desync attacks | **MODERATE** | < 0.14.10 | 0.14.10 | Integer Overflow / Request Smuggling |
| 4 | **CVE-2021-32715** / GHSA-f3pg-qwvg-p99c / RUSTSEC-2021-0078 | Lenient `Content-Length` parsing accepts `+` prefix, enabling request smuggling with non-lenient proxies | **LOW** | < 0.14.10 | 0.14.10 | Request Smuggling |
| 5 | **RUSTSEC-2022-0022** / GHSA-f67m-9j94-qv9j | Unsound use of `mem::uninitialized()` to create `httparse::Header` (contains references); undefined behavior | **HIGH** | < 0.14.12 | 0.14.12 | Memory Safety / Soundness |
| 6 | **CVE-2017-18587** / GHSA-q89x-f52w-6hj2 / RUSTSEC-2017-0002 | Header values not filtered for `\r`/`\n`, allowing response/request splitting via unsanitized user input | **MODERATE** | < 0.9.18, 0.10.0 – < 0.10.2 | 0.9.18 / 0.10.2 | Header Injection |
| 7 | **CVE-2016-10932** / GHSA-9xjr-m6f3-v5wm / RUSTSEC-2016-0002 | No TLS hostname verification on Windows (HTTPS MitM) | **MODERATE** | < 0.9.4 | 0.9.4 | TLS / MitM |

---

## Security Posture Notes

1. **Recurring vulnerability theme — HTTP request smuggling / desync.** Four of seven advisories (CVE-2020-35863, CVE-2021-21299, CVE-2021-32714, CVE-2021-32715) relate to HTTP/1.1 parsing leniency that enables request smuggling. This reflects hyper's position as a low-level HTTP implementation where spec-compliance edge cases carry outsized risk when deployed behind reverse proxies.

2. **All known vulnerabilities have published fixes.** The most recent fix (RUSTSEC-2022-0022) was addressed in **v0.14.12**. Users on **≥ 0.14.12** are not affected by any currently disclosed advisory. The current stable release series is **1.x**, which rewrote significant portions of the HTTP stack and is not covered by any of these advisories.

3. **Massive blast radius.** With ~637M total downloads and ~131M recent downloads, hyper is one of the most-depended-upon crates in the Rust ecosystem. Transitive consumers (via `reqwest`, `axum`, `tonic`, etc.) may not realize they depend on hyper. Supply-chain scanning should resolve transitive dependency versions.

4. **Active maintenance and security process.** The hyperium team uses GitHub Security Advisories, coordinates with RustSec, and has a documented security policy. Response-to-disclosure timelines have been reasonable (days to weeks).

5. **Soundness fix (RUSTSEC-2022-0022) is notable.** Use of `mem::uninitialized()` for a type containing references is instant UB per Rust's memory model. While practical exploitability depends on compiler behavior, this is a correctness/soundness defect independent of attacker input. It underscores the importance of auditing `unsafe` usage even in well-maintained crates.

6. **Legacy versions (< 0.12) carry unpatched historical issues.** The Windows hostname-verification flaw (CVE-2016-10932) and header-injection flaw (CVE-2017-18587) affect very old releases. Any project still pinned to 0.9.x–0.11.x should urgently upgrade.

---

## Key Dependencies & Ecosystem Context

| Dependency | Role | Security Relevance |
|---|---|---|
| `httparse` | HTTP/1.1 header parsing | RUSTSEC-2022-0022 involved interaction with `httparse::Header` type; `httparse` itself has had advisories (e.g., RUSTSEC-2024-0373) |
| `http` (crate) | Shared HTTP types (`Request`, `Response`, `HeaderMap`) | Foundational type crate; changes can affect hyper's behavior |
| `tokio` | Async runtime | hyper 0.14+ and 1.x are tightly coupled to tokio for I/O |
| `h2` | HTTP/2 implementation | Used by hyper for HTTP/2 support; has its own advisory history (e.g., CVE-2024-32650 rapid-reset) |
| `hyper-util` / `hyper-tls` / `hyper-rustls` | Companion crates (1.x era) | TLS configuration and higher-level connectors moved here in hyper 1.x; hostname verification and TLS posture now depend on these |

---
